title: Prabha Energy Ltd - 544379 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Prabha Energy's maiden call: gas sales still ~20,000 cubic meters/day via cascades; pipeline connectivity by Jan-Mar 2027 is the key trigger for ramp-up.
summary.overview: Management hosted its maiden earnings call for Q2 FY27 and H1 FY27, focused largely on the business model and development timelines rather than reported numbers. Current gas sales are small, around 20,000 cubic meters per day, through cascades, pending grid connectivity. Management expects a significant revenue step-up from FY28, with North Karanpura and Jharia pipeline connections due by March 2027 and January 2027 respectively. No quantified P&L figures for the quarter were given on the call, and the company said net profit for FY27 so far exceeds full-year FY26 profit. Capex for Jharia's remaining 47 wells is pegged above INR 500 crore, to be funded roughly 50:50 equity and debt/internal accruals.

financial_highlights.metric: Net profit H1 FY27 vs full-year FY26
financial_highlights.value: Management said FY27 net profit is higher than full-year FY26 profit (no figure given)

financial_highlights.metric: North Karanpura EBITDA margin at optimum capacity

financial_highlights.value: less than four years once at full production (management expectation)

segments.name: North Karanpura CBM block (Jharkhand)
segments.commentary: Approx. 271 sq km; Prabha holds 25% participating interest with ONGC and IOCL; 68 wells drilled and completed but not producing pending grid connection. IOCL's 68 km evacuation pipeline to Urja Ganga is over 60% complete, with commissioning expected by March 2027. Gas sales commenced April 2025.

segments.name: Jharia CBM block (Jharkhand)
segments.commentary: Approx. 26 sq km; Prabha holds 90% revenue/profit share with Bharat Coking Coal Ltd. Eight wells drilled and tested; 47 more planned. Gas breakthrough observed; GAIL has approved connectivity to an ~8 km pipeline to Urja Ganga, targeted for January 2027, with initial production from Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Marginal gas fields (Rajasthan, Jaisalmer)
segments.commentary: Three fields over approx. 100 sq km with estimated gas reserves of around 1.4 bcm. Infrastructure includes a gathering station at Bankia and approx. 15 km of pipeline; focus is on optimising operations and identifying gas marketing opportunities. No production figures given.

guidance_outlook: Jharia pipeline connectivity expected by January 2027, with initial commercial production of 20,000 to 40,000 cubic meters/day from the first eight wells, ramping with additional wells.

North Karanpura production and commercial sales to start once IOCL's pipeline connects (deadline March 2027); initial volumes of a few lakh cubic meters/day, with potential up to 7-8 lakh cubic meters/day per management.
Peak combined production expected above 1.5 MMSCMD (15 lakh cubic meters/day), with peak reached around FY28-FY29 (1.5 to 2 years for Jharia, 1 to 2 years for North Karanpura).
Significant turnover increase expected from FY28 onwards, per management.
Jharia 47-well drilling capex above INR 500 crore from FY28, targeted 50% equity and 50% debt/internal accruals.
capex_capacity: North Karanpura: majority of capex already done; capitalisation continues during test production and will stop once production and sales ramp up post pipeline connection.
Jharia: 8 wells drilled and tested; 47 more wells to be drilled, capex above INR 500 crore starting next financial year.
Jharia pipeline to Urja Ganga (~8 km), PNGRB authorised; GAIL connectivity approved; completion targeted January 2027.
Project lifecycle: management says 5 to 6 years from award to production; awards are for 25 to 30 years, with at least 25 years of production expected.
demand_pricing: Gas is sold under an open price mechanism; rates are benchmarked in USD but payments are generally in INR; gas can be sold via IGX and to any buyer once connected to Urja Ganga.

Management cited Asian gas prices rising from around USD 10.8/MMBtu to around USD 25/MMBtu over about eight months, attributed to Middle East conflict; India's LNG imports exceed 50% of gas consumption and over 60% of LNG comes from Gulf producers.
Current cascade sales are about 20,000 cubic meters/day versus up to 10 lakh cubic meters/day possible via pipeline (per management).
Management says Jharia's small area allows more wells in a smaller footprint, but declined to quantify any EBITDA advantage versus North Karanpura.

qa_highlights.question: What volumes will Jharia and North Karanpura inject initially, and when will both be at peak?
qa_highlights.answer: Jharia initial commercial output 20,000-40,000 cubic meters/day from eight wells; NK a few lakh cubic meters/day once connected. Peak production from both put together above 1.5 MMSCMD, reached around FY28-FY29.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin and operating cost per unit can be expected from North Karanpura?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating cost estimated at around 20% and EBITDA of 70% to 75% at optimum capacity, expected in about a year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current status of pipeline connectivity and the incremental sales potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Current cascade sales around 20,000 cubic meters/day; pipeline could carry up to 10 lakh cubic meters/day. Pipeline connectivity is the only bottleneck identified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the North Karanpura participating interest?
qa_highlights.answer: 25% participating interest, 25% share of revenue and expenses, with ONGC and IOCL as partners.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex is needed for Jharia and how will it be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Above INR 500 crore for the balance 47 wells, targeted 50% equity and 50% debt/internal accruals; no partnerships beyond NK under consideration.

qa_highlights.question: What is the payback and cash conversion cycle for these projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said payback under four years once at full production; 5 to 6 years from award to production.

risks_watch: Both pipeline connections (Jharia January 2027, North Karanpura March 2027) are dependent on third parties (GAIL, IOCL); any slippage defers revenue ramp-up.
Revenue is still minimal; management has not given quarterly revenue, EBITDA or PAT figures on the call, and guidance is qualitative.
Capitalisation of North Karanpura expenditure continues during test production; the switch to expensing once sales ramp will affect reported profit.
Jharia capex above INR 500 crore needs an equity raise of about INR 250 crore plus debt or accruals; dilution and leverage to monitor.
Management's statements on Jharia 2 block (PNGRB auction) and additional bids remain uncertain; no bids placed yet.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on long-term growth, with repeated references to FY28 and beyond, but cautious on near-term numbers, which management described as minuscule. Several answers were vague or deferred (e.g., quantifying Jharia's cost advantage, the number of wells to drill, and the timing of additional bids).
key_quotes: Gas sales through cascades are in smaller quantities as we are in the infrastructure development stage and we expect a significant increase in our turnover from FY'28, backed by pipeline connectivity with the national gas grid.
So the only bottleneck as of now we are foreseeing is pipeline connectivity and once this connecting pipeline with Urja Ganga that's the National Grid.
So these projects are awarded for 25 to 30 years and so we can expect production from these wells at least for 25 years.

adds.what: Jharia CBM: 47 additional wells (capex above INR 500 crore), drilling to start FY28
North Karanpura CBM: 68 drilled wells awaiting IOCL 68 km evacuation pipeline to Urja Ganga (over 60% complete)
Jharia CBM: ~8 km pipeline to Urja Ganga (GAIL-approved connectivity), initial production from first 8 wells at 20,000-40,000 cubic m/day

growth.why: Management guides a significant turnover step-up from FY28 and peak combined output above 1.5 MMSCMD by FY29, backed by GAIL-approved Jharia connectivity (Jan 2027), IOCL North Karanpura pipeline (over 60% complete, Mar 2027) and Jharia capex above INR 500 crore, but no quarterly revenue or profit figures were given and current sales are only about 20,000 cubic m/day.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects North Karanpura EBITDA margin of 70% to 75% at optimum capacity with operating cost around 20%, versus minimal current cascade sales of about 20,000 cubic m/day.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: IOCL's 68 km North Karanpura evacuation pipeline is over 60% complete with commissioning by March 2027, and GAIL-approved Jharia ~8 km pipeline targets January 2027, with Jharia initial output of 20,000-40,000 cubic m/day.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Peak combined production expected above 1.5 MMSCMD (15 lakh cubic m/day) by FY28-FY29, up from current cascade sales of about 20,000 cubic m/day once pipelines connect.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Jharia 47 remaining wells need capex above INR 500 crore starting FY28, targeted 50% equity (about INR 250 crore) and 50% debt/internal accruals.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said FY27 net profit already exceeds full-year FY26 profit, but no figures were given and guidance is qualitative, so an upgrade is unquantified.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Both pipeline connections depend on third parties (GAIL January 2027, IOCL March 2027); any slippage defers the ramp-up from FY28 that management is guiding to.

rows.label: Significant turnover step-up from FY28
rows.why: Management guides a significant turnover increase from FY28 as pipelines connect, versus current sales of about 20,000 cubic m/day via cascades.

rows.label: Gas prices rising sharply (Asian LNG USD 10.8 to ~25/MMBtu)
rows.why: Management cited Asian gas prices rising from about USD 10.8 to about USD 25/MMBtu over eight months, with gas sold on an open price mechanism once connected, but prices are not guaranteed to hold.

rows.label: Capitalisation stops, expensing begins post-ramp
rows.when: on pipeline connection (Q4 FY27 to FY28)
rows.why: North Karanpura expenditure is capitalised during test production and will be expensed once sales ramp up after pipeline connection, which will reduce reported profit.

tone.note: Management was confident on long-term FY28-FY29 ramp, pipeline connectivity and 70-75% NK EBITDA margins, but cautious on near-term numbers it called minuscule and vague on Jharia cost advantage, well count and extra bids; analysts pressed on volumes, margins and funding.
